## schedule — timers, and running work on the unit's thread

Does: Runs work repeatedly or once after a delay, and runs work handed over from another thread (a network callback, an awaited task) on the unit's own thread.
Needs: Nothing.

Calls on `ISchedule`:
- `IDisposable Every(TimeSpan interval, Action work)` — Runs `work` every `interval`; dispose to stop.
- `IDisposable After(TimeSpan delay, Action work)` — Runs `work` once after `delay`; dispose to cancel.
- `void Post(Action work)` — Runs `work` on the unit's thread as soon as it is free; safe to call from any thread.

Limits: Timers and posted work run one at a time with every other handler, in order. Intervals shorter than 100 ms are raised to 100 ms. Threads and System.Threading timers are not allowed — use this.
